description:
Companion to closed JMAP-sc1b.71. While auditing for that bead I confirmed three further response-side state fields in crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:

- crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:288   pub query_state: String        (QueryResponse)
- crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:335   pub old_query_state: String    (QueryChangesResponse)
- crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:337   pub new_query_state: String    (QueryChangesResponse)

These are the response-side analogues to since_query_state, which already uses State on the request side (see e.g. crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs:1471, crate-jmap-tasks-client/src/methods/task_notification.rs:118).

RFC 8620 §5.5 and §5.6 describe queryState / oldQueryState / newQueryState as opaque object-type-specific state strings — the same opaque-token shape that motivates the State newtype. JMAP-sc1b.71 closed the same gap for state / old_state / new_state on GetResponse, ChangesResponse, SetResponse, and EmailImportResponse.

Fix is mechanical: String → State, add State to the use list. Wire format is preserved (State is #[serde(transparent)]). All workspace .query_state / .old_query_state / .new_query_state reads should keep compiling via State's PartialEq<&str> and AsRef<str> impls — verify with cargo test --workspace after the change.

Why P2: SemVer-affecting and the JMAP-sc1b.71 precedent makes the engineering case identical. Cheap to fix now while crates are unpublished; expensive after.
title: Follow-up: 3 query_state sites in jmap-types use String while State newtype exists
